papers.title: GRADPlace: Geometry-Based Routing-Augmented Differentiable Placement for Routability Optimization
authors: Xurong Shen, Xueyan Zhao, Zhipeng Huang, Chaoyu Xing, Biwei Xie
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.27287v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Routability-driven placement needs gradients that show how cell movement redistributes routing demand. Cell inflation exploits routing feedback only indirectly, and differentiable methods rely on black-box congestion predictors or on virtual-cell congestion fields frozen between routing updates. We present GRADPlace, which represents probability-weighted candidate routes as movable horizontal and vertical segments. Routing feedback sets their probabilities, while their geometry and expected demand evolve with cell coordinates. An electrostatic routing objective propagates gradients through this geometry to connected cells, complementing cell inflation. papers.title: Mind the Delta: Early Pruning of RTL Variants for Agentic Hardware Optimization
authors: Siyang Cai, Cangyuan Li, Haoyu Gao, Kun Wang, Mochen Li, Yilin Zhong, Ke Xu, Yinhe Han, Ying Wang
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.27035v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous coding agents powered by large language models (LLMs) now write diverse microarchitectural variants of existing register-transfer level (RTL) designs at high throughput, shifting the primary bottleneck of agentic RTL optimization onto logic synthesis. Commercial toolchains take hours per variant, creating an acute compute asymmetry between proposing and evaluating variants. Existing fast evaluators falter in this regime. Subtle RTL edits trigger nonlinear synthesis shifts that learned predictors and coding agents cannot resolve, while synthesis proxies at reduced effort either alter the optimization trajectory or retain most of its runtime. papers.title: Enabling Spatially Fine-Grained DVFS in Neural Processing Units for Energy-Efficient LLM Serving
authors: Yuqi Xue, Jerry Wu, Corey Yu, Jian Huang
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2607.16473v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: As neural processing units (NPUs) evolve rapidly to accommodate the ever-increasing compute demand of large language models (LLMs), their power consumption is becoming a limiting factor. Our study shows that using dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) to exploit the service-level objective (SLO) slacks is a promising way to improve NPU energy efficiency for LLM services. And as tensor operators in LLMs exhibit diverse bottlenecks across NPU components, it is desirable to configure the frequency separately for each component to maximize their energy efficiency.

papers.title: Cruella: A Unified Microscaling and Floating-Point Dot-Product Unit for LLM Inference on FPGAs
authors: Jinho Yang, Taehyeong Kim, Mincheol Cha, Hyeoncheol Kim, Donggeun Kim, Nahye Kim, Yujin Lee, Ryeowook Ko, Woong Gyu Park, Jiwoong Park, Junsoo Kim, Tae-Hyoung Kim, Yongjun Park, Seongmin Hong, Joo-Young Kim
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.27323v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The number formats that accelerators execute natively are fixed at fabrication, yet large language model (LLM) checkpoints are released with MXFP4 weights in the Microscaling (MX) formats standardized in 2023. FPGAs adopt new formats through bitstreams. However, to the best of our knowledge, no deployed FPGA LLM accelerator executes MXFP4 weights alongside BF16 products. We characterize the decoding of MXFP4 checkpoints, whose layers alternate between MXFP4$\times$BF16 products and BF16$\times$BF16 products of attention and BF16 layers. With a BF16 KV cache, BF16$\times$BF16 products take 56%-77% of the datapath time, during which a separate MXFP4 unit idles. papers.title: Rethinking ANNS on Commodity PIM: PIM-Native Vector Search with Cooperative Filtering
authors: Dawei Guo, Yizou Chen, Fan Yang, Hui Li, Ming-Chang Yang
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.27010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) is a key primitive in modern data-intensive systems, and its memory-bound vector-scanning stage makes processing-in-memory (PIM) a promising acceleration platform. Existing PIM-based ANNS systems largely transplant CPU-oriented distance evaluation and top-$k$ selection onto PIM, introducing arithmetic- and state-heavy operations that poorly match lightweight, isolated PIM cores. To address these mismatches, we present PIVOT, a PIM-native vector search system with cooperative filtering, which thoroughly rethinks how ANNS should be executed on commodity PIM. papers.title: Auto-Scaling Heterogeneous Neural Processing Units for Energy and Cost-Efficient LLM Serving
authors: Yuqi Xue, Jichuan Chang, Jian Huang
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2607.16488v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: To meet the ever-increasing computing demands of large language model (LLM) services, modern cloud platforms have widely deployed neural processing units (NPUs). These NPU chips have been developed and evolved at an incredibly fast pace, this inevitably produces heterogeneous compute pools backed by different versions of NPU chips. Unfortunately, due to the lack of system and architecture support for managing NPU heterogeneity in the cloud, it is unclear how to best utilize heterogeneous NPUs to maximize the energy and cost efficiency for LLM services.
